title: Should dir=auto with no strong characters inherit directionality from parent or be ltr?

labels.name: i18n-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of Internationalization, or tracked by i18n but not needing response.

labels.name: i18n-alreq
labels.description: Notifies Arabic script experts of relevant issues

labels.name: i18n-hlreq
labels.description: Notifies Hebrew script experts of relevant issues

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The HTML spec has for a while (at least since sometime before the refactoring in #9554) said that, in the cases where `dir=auto` determines directionality from the text content of an element (as opposed to the cases where it looks at form control values as it does for text inputs and textarea), the element inherits directionality from the parent when the text content does not have strong characters ("a code point whose bidirectional character type is L, AL, or R").  (See [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#the-dir-attribute).)

For a long time no implementations did this.  As part of [recent directionality changes](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=576815) I shipped this behavior in Chrome 120.  (See [the CL](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/4805163) that made the change.)  This CL changed [one WPT](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/dom/elements/global-attributes/dir_auto-N-EN.html?label=experimental&label=master) which still fails in Safari and Firefox.

We recently got [a bug report](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1521783) about this behavior, with a description of a case that it broke.

My question is:  do we want to revert this behavior in Chrome and change the HTML spec back to the old browser behavior?  Or is what the HTML spec previously described considered the desirable behavior?

cc @fantasai @r12a
